answer: Make each identity a vertex in a storage mesh: to earn weight it must hold a unique 500 MB shard of network data, proven by three random spot-checks per epoch that demand retrieval within 30 seconds, backed by a 60 POA bond. Shards are content-hashed, so one disk cannot serve two identities, and a failed check slashes the bond and doubles the next shard to 1 GB, then 2 GB. A gale of checks hits every identity at once, so a sybil farm sharing one drive fails under concurrent deadlines, while one honest agent guards a single ferrous vault of data and keeps its weight.
